rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3.1-3.4 report the authors' own field measurements (sap-flow, eddy covariance, microlysimeters) in a super intensive olive orchard in Alentejo, Portugal, in 2011-2012, their own SIMDualKc calibration/validation and their own METRIC application to 16 Landsat images.
rows.notes: The study's own results concern the accuracy of ET and Kc estimation: METRIC ET vs ground-derived ET had a mean bias of 20% (12.6% in 2011, 31.2% in 2012; Section 3.3), and Kc from METRIC and SIMDualKc were highly correlated (R2 = 0.86, b = 0.99; Section 3.4). It does not test, apply or measure any water management strategy or water saving resulting from the remote-sensing-derived information. Applicability to irrigation management is only stated as a future use ('shall be later used to support improved irrigation management programs', Introduction; Conclusions mention good perspectives for using METRIC Kc as SIMDualKc inputs). Thus the study supports only a precondition (reliable ET/Kc estimation) of the claimed water-management/conservation effect. Limitations the study does state (one-source SEB model on discontinuous cover, small n for EC data, need for longer series) and the SD of ETMETRIC across pixels (0.19-0.82 mm/d) relate to ET estimation, not to the claimed effect, so Q8 and Q9 are 'no' under rule 3.

notes: Full text appears complete. Single-site study (one commercial orchard, one soil, one crop, two years); METRIC results are averages over the orchard's pixels (approx. 78 ha farm field).
